newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Rawlings wins four-year term.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Rawlings wins four-year term.

text.p: President Jerry Rawlings, who has dominated national life in Ghana for almost two decades, won Ghana's weekend presidential election, the head of the national election commission said on Wednesday.
Kwadwo Afari-Gyan told a news conference Rawlings had received 57.2 percent of votes cast against 39.9 percent for his main rival John Kufuor. This gives Rawlings a final four-year term.
The turnout in Saturday's presidential and parliamentary elections was 76.8 percent.
Afari-Gyan said the results were based on 197 of the West African nation's 200 constituencies.
In the contest for parliament's 200 seats Rawlings's National Democratic Congress won 130 seats and the combined opposition a total of 65. Results were not yet tallied for five seats.
